title: 'La Nevada' at the Jazz Gallery, 1960
summary: Gil recalls playing 'La Nevada' 36 times in six weeks at the Jazz Gallery, then improvising it on record.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: 'La Nevada' was not regulated. We played at a place called the Jazz Gallery on St. Marks and 1st Avenue in 1960. It was the longest job I ever had with a band. We spent six weeks there. So at the end of six weeks we had played 'La Nevada' 36 times. (LAUGHTER). And never liked it. It came out on the record. It was the first time that we'd ever done that, but we'd been playing it so many nights you know. We knew it so well that after a little conference that we had about the order of the solos and how the band was going to come in on the written parts of the thing. I would cue them in. And also they were going to come in and so certain things that if I might think of an idea on the piano they were going to pick it up and use it as a background or something you know. So,
we improvised that. We only played it once. That was, we just came in and played for fifteen minutes and that was it.
